There are two mini projects, each worth **10% of your grade**. Both may be completed individually or
in pairs.

Unlike the homework, a mini project is **not a set of numbered problems**. You are given a question
and a required method, and you decide how to build and present the argument. What you hand in is a
short report with required elements, not answers in order.

| | Out | Due | Repository |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| [**MP1** --- Regression and Simulation](mp01/mp01.qmd) | Mon 3/01 | **Wed 3/17** | [`mp01`](https://github.com/bee-envdata-cornell/mp01) |
| [**MP2** --- Extremes and Model Comparison](mp02/mp02.qmd) | Mon 4/05 | **Fri 5/07** | [`mp02`](https://github.com/bee-envdata-cornell/mp02) |

The linked pages are the full instructions, public so you can read them before the project is
released. **If you are enrolled, work from a fork of the repository** --- that is where the data and
the package environment are.

## General information

- **Fork the project repository.** When a project is released, a link will be posted on
  [Ed Discussion](https://us.edstem.org). Click **Fork** on GitHub to create a copy under your own
  account, then clone your fork. This gives you the package environment and a repository you can
  point at if you need help with your code.
- **Clone your fork, not the original.** You cannot push to `bee-envdata-cornell/mp01`; look for
  `<your-username>/mp01`. If you clone the wrong one, re-clone your fork and move any edited files
  across --- nothing is lost.
- **Submit a PDF to Gradescope** by 9:00pm Eastern on the due date, **with pages tagged**. Untagged
  submissions take a non-negotiable 10% deduction.
- **Pairs**: exactly one member submits, and it is the submitter's responsibility to add the other
  member in Gradescope. Put both names and NetIDs on the first page. See
  [group work](../policies/groups.qmd) for what is expected of a pair.
- You do **not** have to use the provided notebook, and you do **not** need to submit code. Your
  notebook or scripts should be in your repository in case there are questions.

## How they are graded

Each project is graded by Prof. Srikrishnan against the [standard rubrics](../policies/rubric.qmd),
applied to the required elements rather than to sections. The report is graded on whether each
element is **present and convincing**, not on whether it appears under a particular heading.

Two things worth knowing before you start:

- **A model with no assumptions stated earns nothing for that element.** This is the single thing the
  course most wants you to stop doing.
- **A check that fails, honestly reported and diagnosed, earns full credit.** A check that fails and
  is not noticed earns none. You are not being graded on having a model that works.

Full logistics are on the [project policies page](../policies/projects.qmd).
